text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x, y) ::: x is allowed in y.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in x.
MonthlyRent(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at x is y.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: The security deposit at x is y.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
More(x, y) ::: x is more than y.
Owner(x, y) ::: x is the owner of y.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(pet, x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → DepositRequired(x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → (SecurityDeposit(x, y) ↔ (y = MonthlyRent(x, z)) ⊕ More(y, z))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to the monthly rent at a managed building or more.
Cat(fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
MonthlyRent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
More(2000, 1500) ::: $2000 is more than $1500.
(Owner(tom, fluffy) ∧ Allowed(fluffy, x) ∧ More(SecurityDeposit(x, y), 1500)) → ¬Rent(tom, x) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(pet, x) → ∀y (Pet(y) → Allowed(y, x))) ::: If a managed building allows pets, then people are allowed to move in with a pet.
Conclusion:
Allowed(tom, oliveGarden) ::: Tom is allowed to move into an apartment in The Olive Garden with Fluffy.
